translations.idiomatic: Zongbi sighed and said, "What is past cannot be undone."

sentences.zh: 乃班師。

translations.literal: Thereupon they withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Then he ordered the withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 彀英殿，且戰且卻，遂達秦中。

translations.literal: Gouying served as rear guard, fighting as he retreated, and thus reached Qinzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Gouying covered the retreat, fighting as he withdrew, and brought the army safely into Qinzhong.

sentences.zh: 齊國初廢，元帥右監軍撒離喝馳驛撫治諸郡，至同州，故齊觀察使李世輔出迎，陽墜馬稱折臂，歸。

translations.literal: When Qi was first abolished, the marshal and right military commissioner Saliha rode post-horses to pacify and govern the commanderies; reaching Tong Prefecture, the former Qi inspection commissioner Li Shifu came out to welcome him, feigned a fall from his horse and claimed a broken arm, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi state was abolished, Marshal Saliha, right military commissioner, galloped by post road to settle the commanderies. At Tongzhou the former Qi inspector Li Shifu came out to welcome him, pretended to fall from his horse with a broken arm, and went home.

sentences.zh: 撒離喝入城，世輔詐使通判獻甲，以壯士十人，被甲上査事，世輔自壁後突出，執撒離喝。

translations.literal: Saliha entered the city; Shifu falsely had the vice-prefect present armor; with ten stalwart men in armor they went up to inspect affairs; Shifu burst out from behind the wall and seized Saliha.
translations.idiomatic: Saliha entered the city. Shifu had the vice-prefect offer armor on the pretext of a gift, sent ten armed men up to "inspect," then sprang from behind the wall and seized him.

sentences.zh: 彀英方索馬於外，變起倉卒，不得入。

translations.literal: Gouying was just seeking a horse outside; the change arose in sudden haste and he could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Gouying was outside looking for a mount; the revolt broke too suddenly for him to get in.

sentences.zh: 城門已閉，皆有兵衛，至東門，合荅雅領騎三十餘，與彀英遇，遂斬門者出。

translations.literal: The city gates were already closed and all had guards; reaching the east gate he met Hedaya leading a little more than thirty horsemen; they cut down the gatekeepers and went out.
translations.idiomatic: The gates were shut and guarded, but at the east gate Gouying met Hedaya with a little over thirty riders; they killed the gate guards and broke out.

sentences.zh: 而世輔擁眾自西門出，彀英與合荅雅襲之，一進一退以綴世輔，使不得速。

translations.literal: Shifu led his crowd out through the west gate; Gouying and Hedaya struck them, advancing and retreating to delay Shifu and keep him from going fast.
translations.idiomatic: Shifu led his men out the west gate; Gouying and Hedaya harried them, advancing and falling back to slow his flight.

sentences.zh: 世輔慮救兵至，乃要撒離喝與之盟，勿使追之。

translations.literal: Shifu, fearing relief troops would arrive, then demanded Saliha covenant with him not to let pursuers follow.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing relief, Shifu forced Saliha to swear that no pursuit would follow.

sentences.zh: 留撒離喝於道側，彀英識其聲，與騎而歸。

translations.literal: He left Saliha at the roadside; Gouying recognized his voice and rode off with him in return.
translations.idiomatic: He left Saliha by the road; Gouying knew his voice, rode to him, and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 除安遠大將軍，攝太原尹，四境鹹治，兼攝河東南、北兩路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant, acting Taiyuan prefect; the four circuits were all well governed; he also concurrently held supreme command of the Hedong South and North Route armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant and acting prefect of Taiyuan; the four circuits were well ordered, and he also held overall command of the Hedong South and North armies.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以河南、陝西與宋，已而複取之，師至耀州。

translations.literal: The court ceded Henan and Shaanxi to Song; before long it took them back again; the army reached Yao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court had yielded Henan and Shaanxi to the Song, then recovered them; the army advanced to Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 宋人每旦出城，張旗閱隊，抵暮而還。

translations.literal: Each dawn the Song people came out of the city, raised banners, and reviewed troops, returning at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Every morning the Song garrison marched out to raise banners and drill, returning at dusk.

sentences.zh: 道隘，騎不得逞。

translations.literal: The road was narrow and cavalry could not deploy.
translations.idiomatic: The road was too narrow for cavalry to charge freely.

sentences.zh: 彀英請兵五百，薄暮先使五十人趨山巔，令之曰：「旦日視敵出，舉幟指其所向。」

translations.literal: Gouying requested five hundred troops; at dusk he first sent fifty men to rush the mountaintop and ordered them: "At dawn watch for the enemy to come out; raise banners pointing toward where they go."
translations.idiomatic: Gouying asked for five hundred men and at dusk sent fifty to the ridge with orders: "At dawn, when the enemy marches out, raise a banner showing their direction."

sentences.zh: 乃以餘兵伏山谷間。

translations.literal: He then stationed the remaining troops in ambush among the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: He hid the rest in the valleys.

sentences.zh: 明日，城中人出閱如前，山巔旗舉，伏兵發，宋兵爭馳入城。

translations.literal: Next day the people in the city came out to review as before; the banners on the mountaintop were raised; the ambush troops sprang forth; Song troops struggled to race into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the garrison drilled as usual; the signal went up, the ambush closed in, and the Song troops broke for the gate.

sentences.zh: 彀英麾軍登城，拔宋幟，立金軍旗幟。

translations.literal: Gouying commanded the army up onto the walls, pulled down Song banners, and raised Jin military banners.
translations.idiomatic: Gouying stormed the wall, tore down Song banners, and raised the Jin colors.

sentences.zh: 宋兵後者望見之不敢入，遂降，城中人亦降。

translations.literal: Song troops behind who saw this did not dare enter; they thereupon submitted, and the people within the city also submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The rear of the Song column, seeing the Jin flag on the wall, dared not enter and surrendered; the townspeople submitted as well.

sentences.zh: 宋吳玠擁重兵據涇州，涇原以西多應之。

translations.literal: The Song Wu Jie held heavy forces at Jing Prefecture; west of Jingyuan many responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jie held a large Song force at Jingzhou, and districts west of Jingyuan rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 元帥撒離喝欲退守京兆，俟河南、河東軍。

translations.literal: The marshal Saliha wished to withdraw and hold Chang'an, waiting for the Henan and Hedong armies.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Saliha wanted to fall back on Chang'an and wait for the Henan and Hedong columns.

sentences.zh: 彀英曰：「我退守，吳玠必取鳳翔、京兆、同、華，據潼關，吾屬無類矣。」

translations.literal: Gouying said: "If we withdraw to defend, Wu Jie will surely take Fengxiang, Chang'an, Tong, and Hua, hold Tong Pass, and none of us will survive."
translations.idiomatic: Gouying said, "If we pull back, Wu Jie will take Fengxiang, Chang'an, Tong, and Hua, seize Tong Pass, and none of us will get out alive."

sentences.zh: 撒離喝曰：「計將安出？」

translations.literal: Saliha said: "What plan will come forth?"
translations.idiomatic: Saliha asked, "What do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 彀英曰：「事危矣，不如速戰。

translations.literal: Gouying said: "The situation is perilous; better to fight swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Gouying answered, "The danger is acute—we must fight at once.

sentences.zh: 我軍陣涇之南原，宋兵必自西原來。

translations.literal: Our army should array on the south plain of Jing; the Song army is sure to come from the west plain.
translations.idiomatic: Draw up on the south plain of Jing; the Song are sure to come from the west plain.

sentences.zh: 彀英與斜補出各以選騎五百摧其兩翼，元帥當其中擊之，可以得志。」

translations.literal: Gouying and Xiebuchu each with five hundred picked horsemen should crush their two wings; the marshal should strike their center and success can be attained."
translations.idiomatic: Gouying and Xiebuchu, each with five hundred picked riders, should break both wings while the marshal hits the center—that will win the day."

sentences.zh: 監軍拔離速曰：「二子當其左右，拔離速願當其中。

translations.literal: Military commissioner Balisu said: "Let the two lads take their flanks; Balisu is willing to take the center.
translations.idiomatic: Military commissioner Balisu said, "Let the two young men take the wings; I will take the center myself.

sentences.zh: 元帥據岡阜，多張旗幟為疑兵，可以得志。」

translations.literal: The marshal should hold the hill heights, deploy many banners as dummy troops, and success can be attained."
translations.idiomatic: The marshal should hold the heights, plant many banners as a decoy, and we can still prevail."

sentences.zh: 撒離喝從之。

translations.literal: Saliha followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Saliha agreed.

sentences.zh: 吳玠兵果自西原來，彀英、斜補出擊其左右，自旦至午，吳玠左右軍少退，拔離速當其前衝擊之，遂敗玠軍，僵屍枕藉，大澗皆滿。

translations.literal: Wu Jie's army indeed came from the west plain; Gouying and Xiebuchu struck their left and right; from morning to noon Wu Jie's left and right armies slightly withdrew; Balisu met their front and charged them; he thus defeated Jie's army; corpses lay piled upon one another and the great stream was filled.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jie came from the west plain as predicted. Gouying and Xiebuchu shattered both wings; by noon his flanks were giving way and Balisu drove the center. Wu Jie's army was broken; corpses choked the ravine.

sentences.zh: 自此蜀人喪氣，不敢複出，關、陝遂定。

translations.literal: From this the people of Shu lost heart and did not dare come out again; Tong and Shaanxi were thereupon secured.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Shu commanders lost heart and dared not march out again; Tong and Shaanxi were secured.

sentences.zh: 曆行台吏部工部侍郎，從宗弼巡邊，遷刑部尚書，轉元帥左都監。

translations.literal: He passed through the offices of vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and of Works under the Branch Secretariat, followed Zongbi on border tours, was promoted to Minister of Justice, and transferred to left marshal of the commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of Personnel and of Works on the Branch Secretariat, accompanied Zongbi on frontier tours, rose to Minister of Justice, and became left marshal under the commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，遷右監軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he was promoted to right military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande he was made right military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元帥府罷，改山西路統軍使，領西南、西北兩路招討兵馬，坐無功，降臨海軍節度使，曆平陽、太原尹。

translations.literal: When the commander-in-chief's office was abolished he was changed to Shaanxi Route supreme commander, commanding the southwest and northwest pacification armies; for sitting without achievement he was demoted to military commissioner of the Linhai Army and passed through prefect of Pingyang and Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the marshalate was abolished he became Shaanxi Route supreme commander over the southwest and northwest pacification forces; for lack of results he was reduced to Linhai military commissioner and later served as prefect of Pingyang and Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 正隆末，為中都留守，兼西北面都統，討契丹撒八，駐軍歸化州。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenglong he was central capital military governor, concurrently northwest frontier supreme commander, suppressing the Khitan Saba, and encamped at Guihua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenglong he was military governor of the central capital and northwest frontier supreme commander, campaigning against the Khitan Saba from a base at Guihua.

sentences.zh: 大定元年十一月，彀英以軍至中都，同知留守璋請至府議事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Dading, Gouying reached the central capital with his army; Associate Military Governor Zhang requested him to come to the prefectural office to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Dading, Gouying marched to the central capital; Associate Military Governor Zhang asked him to the yamen to consult on affairs.

sentences.zh: 彀英疑璋有謀，乃陽許諾，排節仗若將往者，遂率騎從出施仁門，駐兵通州。

translations.literal: Gouying suspected Zhang harbored a plot; he falsely assented, arrayed ceremonial staff as if about to go, then led his mounted followers out through Shiren Gate and encamped at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting a trap, Gouying feigned agreement, paraded his guard of honor as if setting out, then led his cavalry out Shiren Gate and encamped at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 見世宗於三河。

translations.literal: He met the Shizong at Sanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Shizong at Sanhe.

sentences.zh: 詔彀英以便宜規措河南、陝西、山東邊事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Gouying to dispose of Henan, Shaanxi, and Shandong frontier affairs as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: An edict empowered him to handle Henan, Shaanxi, and Shandong frontier matters as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，至南京，遂複汝、潁、嵩等州縣，授世襲猛安。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year he reached Nanjing and recovered Ru, Ying, Song, and other prefectures and counties; he was granted a hereditary meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year's first month he reached Nanjing and recovered Ru, Ying, Song, and other districts; he received a hereditary meng'an.

sentences.zh: 入拜平章政事，罷為東京留守，未行，改濟南尹。

translations.literal: He entered court and was appointed Grand Councillor of State; he was dismissed and made Eastern Capital military governor; before he set out he was changed to Jinan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Grand Councillor, was removed to Eastern Capital military governor, and before he departed was reassigned as Jinan prefect.

sentences.zh: 初，彀英宿將恃功，在南京頗瀆貨，不恤軍民。

translations.literal: At first Gouying, a veteran general relying on past merit, at Nanjing was quite corrupt in goods and did not care for soldiers and people.
translations.idiomatic: By then Gouying, an old general trading on past merit, was openly venal at Nanjing and indifferent to troops and civilians.

sentences.zh: 詔使問以邊事，彀英不答，謂詔使曰：「爾解何事，待我到闕奏陳。」

translations.literal: When an edict envoy inquired about frontier affairs Gouying did not answer and said to the envoy: "What do you understand of such matters? Wait until I reach court to report in person."
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial envoy asked about the frontier he refused to answer and told the man, "What do you know of such things? I shall report to the throne myself when I arrive."

sentences.zh: 及召入，竟無一語及邊事者。

translations.literal: When he was summoned in he ultimately did not speak a single word about frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he never mentioned the frontier at all.

sentences.zh: 在相位多自專，己所欲輒自奏行之。

translations.literal: In the chancellorship he often acted on his own authority; whatever he himself wanted he forthwith memorialized and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: As councillor he often acted on his own, memorializing and executing whatever he wished.

sentences.zh: 除留守，輒忿忿不接賓客，雖近臣往亦不見。

translations.literal: On receiving the military governorship he was resentful and would not receive guests; even close officials who went to see him he also would not meet.
translations.idiomatic: Made military governor again, he sulked and refused visitors, turning away even intimate courtiers.

sentences.zh: 上怒，遂改濟南。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and thereupon changed him to Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered and transferred him to Jinan.

sentences.zh: 上數之曰：「朕念卿父有大功于國，卿舊將亦有功，故改授此職，卿宜知之。

translations.literal: The emperor reproved him, saying: "I bear in mind that your father had great merit for the state and that you as an old general also have merit; therefore I have reassigned you this post—you should understand this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him: "I remember your father's great service to the state, and you too have earned merit as an old commander—that is why I have given you this post. You should understand that.

sentences.zh: 若複不悛，非但不保官爵，身亦不能保也。」

translations.literal: If you again do not repent, not only will you not keep office and enfeoffment—you will not even keep your person safe.
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse to mend your ways, you will lose more than rank and title—you will not keep your life.

sentences.zh: 彀英頓首謝。

translations.literal: Gouying bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Gouying kowtowed in acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 久之，改平陽尹，致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time he was changed to Pingyang prefect and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was made prefect of Pingyang and retired.

sentences.zh: 起為西京留守，以母憂去官。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Western Capital military governor and left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Western Capital military governor but left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官起複。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to the same post.

sentences.zh: 俄複為東京，曆上京，詔曰：「上京王業所起，風俗日趨詭薄，宗室聚居，號為難治。

translations.literal: Soon he was again Eastern Capital military governor, then passed through Superior Capital; an edict said: "The Superior Capital is where the royal enterprise arose; customs daily trend toward artifice and meanness; the imperial clan is massed together, and it is called hard to govern.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon Eastern Capital military governor again, then Superior Capital; an edict ran: "The Superior Capital is where the dynasty began; manners grow daily more false and mean; the imperial clan is crowded there, and it is said to be hard to govern.

sentences.zh: 卿元老大臣，眾所聽服，當正風俗，檢制宗室，持以大體。」

translations.literal: You are an elder statesman whom all heed and obey; you should rectify customs, restrain the imperial clan, and uphold the larger principles."
translations.idiomatic: You are an elder whom all respect—set the tone, restrain the clan, and hold to the larger good."

sentences.zh: 十五年。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Dading.

sentences.zh: 致仕。

translations.literal: He retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He then retired from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，史臣上《太宗》、《睿宗實錄》，上曰：「當時舊人親見者，惟彀英在。」

translations.literal: After a long time the historiographers submitted the Veritable Records of Taizong and Ruizong; the sovereign said, "Of the old men who saw those times with their own eyes, only Gouying remains."
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward the historiographers presented the Veritable Records of Taizong and Ruizong; the emperor said, "Of those who witnessed those days, only Gouying is still alive."

sentences.zh: 詔修撰溫蒂罕締達往北京就其家問之，多更定焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the compiler Wendihan Dida to go to Beijing and question him at his home, and many passages were revised accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the compiler Wendihan Dida to visit Gouying at Beijing and consult him, and many passages were revised on that basis.

sentences.zh: 十九年，薨，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died, at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 最前後以功被賞者十有一，金為兩二百五十，銀為兩六千五百，絹為疋八百，綿為兩二千，馬三百十有四，牛羊六千五百，奴婢百三十人。

translations.literal: In all, for merit he was rewarded on eleven occasions: two hundred fifty liang of gold, six thousand five hundred liang of silver, eight hundred bolts of silk, two thousand liang of cotton, three hundred fourteen horses, six thousand five hundred cattle and sheep, and one hundred thirty slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Over his career he received eleven major rewards for merit: two hundred fifty liang of gold, six thousand five hundred of silver, eight hundred bolts of silk, two thousand liang of cotton, three hundred fourteen horses, six thousand five hundred head of cattle and sheep, and one hundred thirty slaves.

sentences.zh: 母弟 麻吉

translations.literal: Maternal younger brother Maji
translations.idiomatic: Maternal younger brother Maji

sentences.zh: 麻吉，銀朮可之母弟也。

translations.literal: Maji was the maternal younger brother of Yinzhuke.
translations.idiomatic: Maji was Yinzhuke's maternal younger brother.

sentences.zh: 年十五，隸軍中，從破高麗兵，下甯江州，平系遼女直，克黃龍府，皆身先力戰，以功為謀克，繼領猛安。

translations.literal: At age fifteen he entered the army, followed in defeating Goryeo troops, taking Ningjiang Prefecture, pacifying Jurchen registered under the Liao, and capturing Huanglong Prefecture—always leading in person and fighting fiercely—and for merit was made a meng'an and later headed a meng'an command.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he joined the army, helped defeat Goryeo, take Ningjiang, pacify Liao-registered Jurchen, and capture Huanglong, always fighting in the van; for merit he became a meng'an and later commanded one.

sentences.zh: 破奚兵千餘。

translations.literal: He defeated more than a thousand Xi troops.
translations.idiomatic: He routed over a thousand Xi troops.

sentences.zh: 自斡魯古攻下鹹、信、瀋州及東京諸城，麻吉皆有功。

translations.literal: From Wolugu's attacks taking Xian, Xin, Shen prefectures and the cities of the Eastern Capital, Maji had merit in each.
translations.idiomatic: In Wolugu's campaigns that took Xian, Xin, Shen, and the Eastern Capital cities, Maji distinguished himself throughout.

sentences.zh: 都統杲取中京，與稍合、胡拾答別降楚里迪部，屯兵高州。

translations.literal: When the commander-in-chief Gao took the Central Capital, he with Shaoge and Hushida separately received the submission of the Chulidi tribe and encamped at Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When commander Gao took the Central Capital, he and Shaoge and Hushida won over the Chulidi tribe and camped at Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 以兵援蒙刮勃堇，大破敵兵，變敗恩州兵五萬人。

translations.literal: With troops he aided Mengua Bojin, badly defeated enemy forces, and again defeated fifty thousand troops of En Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He reinforced Mengua Bojin, routed the enemy, and again shattered fifty thousand Enzhou troops.

sentences.zh: 討平遼人聚中京山谷者，降三千餘人。

translations.literal: He suppressed Liao people gathered in the valleys of the Central Capital and received the submission of more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Liao bands hiding in the Central Capital hills and accepted the surrender of more than three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 戰于高州境上，伏矢射之中目，遂卒。

translations.literal: Fighting on the border of Gaozhou, he was struck in the eye by an arrow from ambush and died.
translations.idiomatic: In battle on the Gaozhou frontier an ambush arrow struck his eye and he died.

sentences.zh: 麻吉大小三十余戰，所至皆捷。

translations.literal: Maji fought in more than thirty engagements large and small and was victorious wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: Maji fought more than thirty battles, large and small, and was victorious in every one.

sentences.zh: 皇統中，贈銀青光祿大夫，諡毅敏。

translations.literal: During Huangtong he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Glory with Silver Seal and given the posthumous title Yimin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huangtong he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Glory with Silver Seal, with the posthumous title Yimin.

sentences.zh: 子沃側。

translations.literal: His son was Woce.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Woce.

sentences.zh: 子 沃側

translations.literal: Son Woce
translations.idiomatic: Son Woce

sentences.zh: 沃側，年十七，隸軍中，從拔離速擊遼將馬五，敗之。

translations.literal: Woce, at age seventeen, entered the army and followed Balisu in attacking the Liao general Ma Wu and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Woce was seventeen when he joined the army; with Balisu he attacked the Liao general Ma Wu and routed him.

sentences.zh: 麻吉死，領其職。

translations.literal: When Maji died he took over his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Maji died he succeeded to his command.

sentences.zh: 宗望伐宋，至河上。

translations.literal: Zongwang attacked Song and reached the river.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang invaded Song and reached the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 宋兵屯於河外，以二舟來伺我師，乃遣沃側率勇士數輩，以一舟往迎之，盡俘以還。

translations.literal: Song troops encamped beyond the river and sent two boats to spy on our army; he then sent Woce leading several brave men with one boat to meet them and captured them all and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Song troops camped beyond the river and sent two boats to scout; Woce led a few picked men in one boat to meet them and took every man prisoner.

sentences.zh: 襲康王于江、淮間，沃側皆與焉。

translations.literal: In the raids on the Prince of Kang between the Yangzi and Huai, Woce took part in all of them.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in every strike against the Prince of Kang between the Yangzi and Huai.

sentences.zh: 師還，駐東平。

translations.literal: When the army returned it encamped at Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march the army encamped at Dongping.

sentences.zh: 及廢齊，屯兵河北，招降旁近諸營，多獲畜產兵仗，軍帥嘉之，賞以甲馬。

translations.literal: When Qi was abolished he encamped in Hebei, won over nearby camps, obtained much livestock and weapons, and the army commander praised him and rewarded him with armor and horses.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi was abolished he garrisoned Hebei, won over neighboring camps, seized much livestock and arms, and his commander rewarded him with armor and horses.

sentences.zh: 後攻陝西，為右翼都統，攻城破敵，皆與有功。

translations.literal: Later in the attack on Shaanxi he was right-wing commander-in-chief; in storming cities and defeating the enemy he had a share of merit in each.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning in Shaanxi as right-wing commander-in-chief, he shared in every siege and victory.

sentences.zh: 師還，正授謀克。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was formally appointed meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he received a formal appointment as meng'an.

sentences.zh: 遷華州防禦使，屬關中歲饑，盜賊充斥，沃側募兵討平之，部以無事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to defender of Hua Prefecture; Guanzhong was suffering famine that year and bandits were everywhere; Woce recruited troops and suppressed them, and his district was thereafter untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: Made defender of Huazhou during a famine year in Guanzhong when bandits were rife, he raised troops, suppressed them, and kept his district at peace.

sentences.zh: 郡人列狀丐留，不報。

translations.literal: The people of the commandery submitted a joint petition asking him to stay; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture petitioned to keep him, but the court did not agree.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除迪列部族節度使，改迭刺部。

translations.literal: Before long he was made military commissioner of the Dilie tribal group and then transferred to the Diela group.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made military commissioner of the Dilie tribes, then of the Diela tribes.

sentences.zh: 用廉入為都水使者，秩滿，同知燕京留守事，為西北路招討使。

translations.literal: Through integrity he entered office as commissioner of waterways; when his term ended he became associate military governor of Yanjing and pacification commissioner of the Northwest Route.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for integrity, he became commissioner of waterways; after his term he was associate military governor of Yanjing and pacification commissioner of the Northwest Route.

sentences.zh: 撒八秩滿已數月，冒其俸祿，不即解去，沃側發其事。

translations.literal: Saba's term had ended several months before, yet he fraudulently drew his salary and did not promptly leave office; Woce exposed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Saba's term had ended months earlier, but he kept drawing pay and would not leave; Woce reported it.

sentences.zh: 撒八反，沃側遇害。

translations.literal: When Saba rebelled, Woce was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Saba rebelled, Woce was killed.

sentences.zh: 弟 拔離速

translations.literal: Younger brother Balisu
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Balisu

sentences.zh: 拔離速，銀朮可弟。

translations.literal: Balisu was the younger brother of Yinzhuke.
translations.idiomatic: Balisu was Yinzhuke's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 天輔六年，宗翰在北安州，將會斜也于奚王嶺，遼兵奄至古北口，使婆盧火、渾黜各領兵二百，擊之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu, Zonghan was at Bei'an Prefecture about to meet Xieyu at Xiwang Ridge when Liao troops suddenly arrived at Gubeikou; he sent Poluhuo and Hunchu each with two hundred troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu, Zonghan was at Bei'an about to meet Xieyu at Xiwang Ridge when Liao forces suddenly appeared at Gubeikou; he sent Poluhuo and Hunchu with two hundred men each to strike them.

sentences.zh: 渾黜請濟師，宗翰欲自往，希尹、婁室曰：「此易與耳，請以千人為公破之。」

translations.literal: Hunchu requested reinforcements; Zonghan wished to go himself; Xiyin and Lou Shi said, "This is easy—please let a thousand men break them for you."
translations.idiomatic: Hunchu asked for reinforcements and Zonghan meant to go himself; Xiyin and Lou Shi said, "This is nothing—a thousand men will do."

sentences.zh: 渾黜以騎士三十人前行，至古北口，遇其遊兵，逐入山谷，遼人以步騎萬余迫戰，亡騎五人，渾黜退據關口。

translations.literal: Hunchu advanced with thirty horsemen, reached Gubeikou, met their scouts, pursued them into a valley, and the Liao with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry pressed the fight; five horsemen were lost and Hunchu withdrew to hold the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Hunchu rode ahead with thirty men to Gubeikou, chased scouts into a valley, and was pressed by over ten thousand Liao foot and horse; he lost five riders and fell back to the pass.

sentences.zh: 希尹、婁室至，拔離速、訛謀罕、胡實海推鋒奮擊，大破之，斬馘甚眾，盡獲甲胄輜重。

translations.literal: When Xiyin and Lou Shi arrived, Balisu, Emohan, and Hushihai drove the van and fought fiercely, routing them badly, beheading and ear-taking in great numbers, and capturing all armor and baggage.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiyin and Lou Shi came up, Balisu, Emohan, and Hushihai led the charge, broke the Liao completely, took many heads, and seized all their armor and baggage.

sentences.zh: 希尹與撒里古獨、裴滿突撚敗其伏兵，殺千餘人，獲馬百餘匹。

translations.literal: Xiyin with Saligudu and Piman Tuanian defeated their ambush troops, killed more than a thousand, and obtained more than a hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyin with Saligudu and Piman Tuanian broke an ambush, killed over a thousand men, and captured more than a hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 婁室拒夏人出陵野嶺，留拔離速以兵二百，據險守之。

translations.literal: Lou Shi held off the Xia coming out from Lingye Ridge and left Balisu with two hundred troops holding the heights.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Shi blocked the Xia at Lingye Ridge and left Balisu with two hundred men on the heights.

sentences.zh: 銀朮可圍太原，近縣先已降，宋軍來救太原者複據太谷、祁縣，拔離速、阿鶻懶複取之。

translations.literal: Yinzhuke besieged Taiyuan; nearby counties had already submitted; Song armies coming to relieve Taiyuan again held Taigu and Qi counties; Balisu and Ahelan took them back.
translations.idiomatic: While Yinzhuke besieged Taiyuan, nearby counties had surrendered; Song relief forces reoccupied Taigu and Qi; Balisu and Ahelan retook them.

sentences.zh: 宋姚古軍隆州穀，拔離速敗之，張灝兵出汾州，又擊走之。

translations.literal: The Song army of Yao Gu was at Longzhou Valley; Balisu defeated it; Zhang Hao's army came out from Fenzhou and he again drove it off.
translations.idiomatic: Balisu routed Yao Gu at Longzhou Valley and drove back Zhang Hao when he marched out of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 天會四年，克太原，拔離速為管勾太原府路兵馬事，複與婁室敗宋兵于文水，遂從宗翰圍汴。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhui Taiyuan was taken; Balisu was made administrator of military affairs of the Taiyuan Prefecture Route, again with Lou Shi defeated Song troops at Wenshui, and then followed Zonghan in besieging Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianhui Taiyuan fell; Balisu was put in charge of Taiyuan Route forces, with Lou Shi beat Song troops at Wenshui, and followed Zonghan to besiege Bian.

sentences.zh: 與銀朮可略地襄、鄧，入均州，還攻唐、蔡、陳三州，皆破之，克潁昌府。

translations.literal: With Yinzhuke he overran the regions of Xiang and Deng, entered Jun Prefecture, returned to attack the three prefectures of Tang, Cai, and Chen, broke them all, and took Yingchang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With Yinzhuke he overran Xiang and Deng, entered Junzhou, stormed Tang, Cai, and Chen, and captured Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 遂與泰欲、馬五襲宋康王于揚州，康王渡江入于建康。

translations.literal: He then with Taiyu and Ma Wu raided the Song Prince of Kang at Yangzhou; the Prince of Kang crossed the river and entered Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: With Taiyu and Ma Wu he raided the Prince of Kang at Yangzhou; the prince crossed the Yangzi to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，遷元帥左都監。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he was transferred to left overseer under the commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he became left overseer under the commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 宗弼再定河南，撒離喝經略陝西，至涇州，拔離速大破宋軍於渭州，渭州、德順軍皆降，陝西平。

translations.literal: When Zongbi again secured Henan, Salihua directed operations in Shaanxi; reaching Jing Prefecture, Balisu badly defeated Song troops at Wei Prefecture; Wei Prefecture and Deshun Army both submitted and Shaanxi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi secured Henan again and Salihua took charge in Shaanxi, Balisu routed the Song at Weizhou; Weizhou and Deshun Army surrendered and Shaanxi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 遷元帥左監軍，加金吾衛上將軍，卒，諡敏定。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left military overseer under the commander-in-chief, promoted to General of the Golden Crow Guard, died, and was given the posthumous title Mindi.
translations.idiomatic: He became left military overseer, was made General of the Golden Crow Guard, died, and received the posthumous title Mindi.

sentences.zh: 習古乃

translations.literal: Xigunai
translations.idiomatic: Xigunai

sentences.zh: 習古乃，亦書作實古乃。

translations.literal: Xigunai is also written Shigunai.
translations.idiomatic: Xigunai is also written Shigunai.

sentences.zh: 嘗與銀朮可俱往遼國取阿疏，還言遼人可取之狀，太祖始決意伐遼矣。

translations.literal: He once went with Yinzhuke to the Liao state to fetch Ashu; on returning he spoke of the condition in which the Liao could be taken, and the Taizu then resolved to attack the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: He once went with Yinzhuke to the Liao to fetch Ashu; on returning he reported that Liao could be taken, and the Taizu resolved to invade.

sentences.zh: 婆盧火取居庸關，蕭妃自古北口出奔，太祖使習古乃追之，不及。

translations.literal: Poluhuo took Juyong Pass; the Xiao consort fled out from Gubeikou; the Taizu sent Xigunai in pursuit but he did not overtake her.
translations.idiomatic: Poluhuo took Juyong Pass; the Xiao consort fled through Gubeikou; the Taizu sent Xigunai after her, but he did not catch her.

sentences.zh: 後為臨潢府軍帥，討平迭刺，其群官率眾降者，請使就領諸部。

translations.literal: Later he was military commander of Linhuang Prefecture, suppressed and pacified Diela, and those tribal officials who led the masses in submission asked that they be allowed to continue leading their tribes on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as military commander of Linhuang, he pacified Diela; submitted tribal leaders asked to keep command of their people in place.

sentences.zh: 太宗賜以空名宣頭及銀牌，使以便宜授之。

translations.literal: The Taizong gave him blank commission documents and a silver tablet and had him appoint people as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong gave him blank commissions and a silver tablet to appoint men as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 獲遼許王莎邏、駙馬都尉蕭乙辛。

translations.literal: He captured the Liao Prince of Xu Shaluo and the imperial son-in-law Xiao Yixin.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the Liao Prince of Xu Shaluo and imperial son-in-law Xiao Yixin.

sentences.zh: 遼梁王雅里在紇里水自立，不知果在何處，至是始知之。

translations.literal: The Liao Prince of Liang Yali had declared himself on the Heli River, and it was not known where he actually was; only at this time was it learned.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao Prince of Liang Yali had set himself up on the Heli River, but his whereabouts had been unknown until now.

sentences.zh: 於是，徙遼降人於泰州，時暑未可徙，習古乃請姑處之嶺西。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liao submitters were to be moved to Taizhou; the heat then made moving impossible, and Xigunai requested they be temporarily settled west of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Liao submitters were to be moved to Taizhou, but the heat made relocation impossible, and Xigunai asked that they be held temporarily west of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 及習古乃築新城于契丹周特城，詔置會平州。

translations.literal: When Xigunai built a new city at the Khitan Zhoute Fortress, an edict established Huiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Xigunai built a new city at the Khitan Zhoute fortress, the court established Huiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 烏虎里部人迪烈、劃沙率部族降，朝廷以撻僕野為本部節度使，烏虎為都監。

translations.literal: Dilie and Huasha of the Wuhuli tribe led their tribal group in submission; the court made Tapuye military commissioner of the native command and Wuhu overseer.
translations.idiomatic: Dilie and Huasha of the Wuhuli tribe submitted; the court made Tapuye military commissioner of the tribe and Wuhu overseer.

sentences.zh: 習古乃封還撻僕野等宣誥，以便宜加撻僕野散官，填空名告身授之，及錄上降附有勞故官八百九十三人，朝廷從之。

translations.literal: Xigunai sealed and returned the commissions of Tapuye and others, and as circumstances required added Tapuye a scattered official rank and filled blank appointment documents to grant them; he also recorded and submitted eight hundred ninety-three former officials who had merit in submitting, and the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: Xigunai returned Tapuye's sealed commissions, promoted Tapuye with a scattered official rank on his own authority, filled blank appointments, and submitted a list of eight hundred ninety-three former officials who had earned merit in the surrender; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 於是，迪烈加防禦使，為本部節度使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Dilie was made defender and military commissioner of the native command.
translations.idiomatic: Dilie was made defender and military commissioner of his tribe.

sentences.zh: 劃沙加諸司使，為節度副使，知迪烈底部事。

translations.literal: Huasha was made commissioner of various offices, deputy military commissioner, and in charge of Dilie's tribal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huasha was made commissioner of various offices, deputy military commissioner, and administrator of Dilie's tribal affairs.

sentences.zh: 撻離答加左金吾衛上將軍，節度副使，知突鞠部事。

translations.literal: Tadida was made General of the Left Golden Crow Guard, deputy military commissioner, and in charge of the Tuju tribe's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tadida was made General of the Left Golden Crow Guard, deputy military commissioner, and administrator of the Tuju tribe.

sentences.zh: 阿枲加觀察使，為本部節度使。

translations.literal: Aqi was made observation commissioner and military commissioner of the native command.
translations.idiomatic: Aqi was made observation commissioner and military commissioner of his tribe.

sentences.zh: 其餘遷授有差。

translations.literal: The rest received transfers and appointments in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Others received promotions and transfers according to rank.

sentences.zh: 以厖葛城地分賜烏虎里、迪烈底二部及契丹人，其未墾者聽任力占射。

translations.literal: Land around Pangge Fortress was divided and granted to the two tribes of Wuhuli and Diliedi and to Khitan; for what was not yet cultivated they were allowed to claim by effort and occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Land around Pangge fortress was divided among the Wuhuli and Diliedi tribes and the Khitan; uncultivated plots could be claimed by whoever cleared them.

sentences.zh: 久之，領鹹州煙火事。

translations.literal: After a long time he oversaw beacon-fire affairs of Xian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he oversaw frontier signals for Xian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天會六年，完顏慎思所部及其餘未置猛安謀克戶口，命習古乃通閱具籍以上。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhui the households under Wanyan Shensi and the remaining meng'an not yet registered were ordered to be fully reviewed by Xigunai and the registers submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhui Xigunai was ordered to review and submit registers for Wanyan Shensi's command and all unregistered meng'an households.

sentences.zh: 天會十年，改南京路軍帥司為東南路都統司，習古乃為都統，移治東京，鎮高麗。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianhui the Nanjing Route military command was changed to the Southeast Route overall command; Xigunai was made overall commander, moved his seat to the Eastern Capital, and garrisoned against Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianhui the Nanjing military command became the Southeast overall command; Xigunai was made overall commander, moved to the Eastern Capital, and watched Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金啟疆土，斡魯、斡魯古方面功最先著，婆盧火、婁室最先封，泰州之邊圉，黃龍之沖要，寄亦重矣。

translations.literal: The encomium says: When Jin opened its territory, Wolu and Wolugu on the frontier had the earliest outstanding merit; Poluhuo and Lou Shi were the earliest enfeoffed; the border of Taizhou and the strategic key of Huanglong—the trust placed there was also weighty.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal runs: When Jin opened its realm, Wolu and Wolugu won the earliest frontier fame; Poluhuo and Lou Shi were the first enfeoffed; the Taizhou border and the strategic key of Huanglong were posts of the heaviest trust.

sentences.zh: 若闍母之勤勞南路，婁室之經營陝西，銀朮可之圍守太原，勞亦至矣。

translations.literal: As for Samar's toil on the southern route, Lou Shi's management of Shaanxi, and Yinzhuke's siege and defense of Taiyuan—their labor also reached the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Samar's labor on the southern front, Lou Shi's work in Shaanxi, and Yinzhuke's long siege of Taiyuan were labors of the same order.

sentences.zh: 斡魯古之不治，闍母之敗，譴罰之亟，諸將慴焉。

translations.literal: Wolugu's misgovernment and Samar's defeat brought swift punishment, and the generals were awed.
translations.idiomatic: Wolugu's misrule and Samar's defeat brought swift punishment, and the generals took heed.

sentences.zh: 夫能以弱小終制強大，其效驗與。

translations.literal: That the small could in the end control the great—this was the proof of it.
translations.idiomatic: That the small could in the end master the great—such was the proof.

sentences.zh: 銀朮可、習古乃觀人之國而知其可伐，古語雲「國有八觀」，善矣夫。

translations.literal: Yinzhuke and Xigunai observed another state's condition and knew it could be attacked; the old saying runs, "A state has eight signs of observation"—well said indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzhuke and Xigunai looked into another realm and knew it could be struck; the ancients said a state has eight signs by which to read it—how apt.
